hints: Look carefully at the names of the products given in the question, they tell you exactly which oxides must appear.
Lead stays as lead(II) and sulfur forms sulfur dioxide, so your skeleton should be $\text{PbS} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_2 + \text{PbO}$ before balancing.
Count oxygen atoms on each side to find how many $\text{O}_2$ molecules you need, remembering that half molecules like $1\frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2$ are allowed in equations.
walkthrough:
**Identify the correct products from the names**

The question tells you the products are sulfur dioxide and lead(II) oxide. That means $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{PbO}$, not $\text{SO}_3$ or $\text{PbO}_2$.

Skeleton equation:
$$\text{PbS} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_2 + \text{PbO}$$

**Check that oxidation states have not changed for lead**

In $\text{PbS}$, Pb is +2. In $\text{PbO}$, Pb is still +2. This fits lead(II) oxide. $\text{PbO}_2$ would be lead(IV) oxide, so it is wrong here.

**Balance the oxygen atoms**

Left side has 2 O atoms per $\text{O}_2$. Right side has 2 O in $\text{SO}_2$ plus 1 O in $\text{PbO}$, total 3 O atoms.

To get 3 O atoms on the left you need $1\frac{1}{2}$ molecules of $\text{O}_2$:
$$\text{PbS} + 1\frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_2 + \text{PbO}$$
Pb and S are already balanced with 1 of each on both sides, so this is the finished equation.

options.A: Incorrect because it gives $\text{PbO}_2$ as a product. That is lead(IV) oxide, but the question clearly states lead(II) oxide, $\text{PbO}$, is formed.
options.B: Incorrect because it gives both wrong products, $\text{SO}_3$ and $\text{PbO}_2$. The question states sulfur dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$) and lead(II) oxide ($\text{PbO}$) are formed.
options.C: Correct because it uses the right products, $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{PbO}$, and is correctly balanced. There are 1 Pb, 1 S and 3 O atoms on each side.
options.D: Incorrect because it gives $\text{SO}_3$ (sulfur trioxide) instead of $\text{SO}_2$. Although $\text{PbO}$ is correct, the sulfur product does not match the question.
